answer: Each agent may propose offers freely, but a trade settles only after both parties lock a refundable stake in a shared ledger and later reveal matching receipts. If an identity defaults or submits conflicting receipts, its stake is slashed and the counterparty is compensated. Splitting one agent into a hundred accounts does not multiply influence: every account must lock its own capital, so a sybil swarm ties up funds and risks losing them. The ember, ledge, and ferrous markets can still welcome newcomers without treating unverified identities as trusted.
